references.text: The same principle that a peace offering eaten on the third day is an abomination (פִּגּוּל), and whoever eats it must bear their sin
The context establishing the rules for when peace offerings and thank offerings are to be eaten - on the same day or within two days
A similar rule that the thank offering must be eaten on the same day, with nothing left until morning
Isaiah uses the word פִּגּוּל (abominable thing) regarding unclean meat, using the same terminology as in Leviticus
Ezekiel uses פִּגּוּל to describe abominable meat that he refuses to eat
The principle of bearing one's own sin (עֲוֺנָהּ תִּשָּׂא) is repeated in connection with sins
The warning about bearing sin by profaning the holy offerings
The concept that an offering must be accepted (יֵרָצֶה) to make atonement for the one who brings it
